title: Engineered PETase-MHETase Chimeras for Ambient Plastic Degradation in Marine Environments
query: Pichia pastoris AND PETase AND MHETase AND SpyTag AND marine

matrix.blue: ≥ 85% mass degradation of 50 um PET films within 72 hours at 25°C
matrix.green: Premature catalytic inactivation under marine ionic strength and salinity (>35 PSU)
matrix.yellow: Pichia pastoris GS115 (AOX1 promoter, continuous fed-batch fermentation)
matrix.purple: Negative vehicle buffer control; Positive wild-type IsPETase reference; Specificity non-polyester control

funnel.tier1: Over 14 million metric tons of microplastics accumulate in oceanic ecosystems annually, threatening marine trophic networks and commercial fisheries.
funnel.tier2: Microbial cutinases and bacterial IsPETase can cleave amorphous PET but exhibit rapid thermal denaturation above 30°C and severe catalytic inhibition in hyper-saline marine water.
funnel.tier3: Current enzymatic depolymerization lacks catalytic processivity because intermediate MHET accumulates and acts as a potent competitive inhibitor of PETase in high-salinity aquatic matrices.
funnel.tier4: We hypothesize that covalent proximity-channeling of an engineered salt-tolerant PETase to MHETase via a flexible peptide linker will accelerate intermediate substrate transfer and achieve complete terephthalate mineralization at ambient marine temperatures.

aims.aim1: Engineer salt-stabilized IsPETase variants via computational Rosetta surface charge re-engineering.
aims.aim2: Construct and express SpyTag-SpyCatcher mediated PETase-MHETase multimeric biocatalytic complexes in Pichia pastoris.
aims.aim3: Quantify real-time degradation kinetics and complete mineralization efficiency on aged marine PET microplastics.

aims_contingencies.aim1_fallback: If Rosetta salt-bridge mutants fail to express solubly, substitute with halo-tolerant cutinase scaffolds derived from marine actinomycetes.
aims_contingencies.aim2_fallback: If covalent SpyTag fusion causes steric hindrance around the catalytic triad, utilize a rigid poly-proline helical spacer.
aims_contingencies.aim3_fallback: If marine biofouling impedes enzyme surface adsorption, incorporate a cellulose-binding domain (CBD) for enhanced substrate anchoring.

control_triad.negative_control: Sterile artificial seawater buffer (35 PSU) and empty-vector pPIC9K transformation supernatant without enzyme.
control_triad.positive_control: Recombinant wild-type Ideonella sakaiensis PETase (IsPETase) tested under standard non-saline 30°C conditions.
control_triad.specificity_control: Incubation of the dual-enzyme chimera with non-target synthetic polymers (Nylon-6,6 and Low-Density Polyethylene).

biotech_risk_matrix.off_target: Nonspecific proteolysis of the flexible linker by endogenous Pichia proteases. Mitigation: Utilize protease-deficient strain SMD1168H.
biotech_risk_matrix.toxicity: Accumulation of terephthalic acid (TPA) causing culture acidification. Mitigation: Continuous pH-stat titration with 1M NaOH.
biotech_risk_matrix.solubility: Irreversible aggregation of chimeric enzymes during high-density secretion. Mitigation: Low-temperature induction at 20°C with sorbitol.
biotech_risk_matrix.biosafety: Environmental release of genetically modified yeast into open coastal waters. Mitigation: Strict cell-free immobilized enzyme formulations.

methodology: The engineered PETase and MHETase coding sequences will be synthesized with codon optimization for Pichia pastoris and cloned into pPIC9K downstream of the alpha-mating factor secretion signal. Linearized plasmids will be electroporated into Pichia pastoris SMD1168H. Fermentation will be conducted in a 5L benchtop bioreactor under methanol-induced AOX1 expression at 20°C. Secreted enzymes will be purified via Ni-NTA chromatography and characterized by SDS-PAGE. Plastic degradation assays will utilize crystalline and amorphous PET coupon films in artificial seawater (35 PSU). Reaction progress will be monitored by reverse-phase HPLC with diode array detection at 240 nm to quantify liberated MHET and terephthalic acid. Polymer surface topological degradation will be verified using field-emission scanning electron microscopy.

impact_data.academic: Establishes structural and thermodynamic principles of multi-enzyme proximity channeling for insoluble solid-liquid biocatalysis in saline environments.
impact_data.economic: Provides a low-energy ambient biocatalytic pathway to recover pure polymer precursors (,200/ton TPA) from marine waste without requiring high-temperature chemical recycling.
impact_data.societal: Mitigates persistent microplastic contamination in coastal marine reserves and aquaculture habitats.

competitor_data.incumbent: High-temperature chemical glycolysis (>200°C, 20 bar): energy-intensive, hazardous solvent waste, incompatible with environmental remediation.
competitor_data.emerging: Free wild-type IsPETase: unstable above 30°C, 80% activity loss at marine salinity, inhibited by intermediate MHET.
competitor_data.proposed: Salt-stabilized, SpyTag-channeled PETase-MHETase biocatalyst: operates directly at 20–25°C in seawater with zero intermediate inhibition.
competitor_data.usp: The first ambient-temperature marine-stable dual enzyme cascade achieving stoichiometric conversion of PET microplastics into soluble monomers in real seawater.

swot.s: Ultra-rapid synergistic depolymerization due to elimination of MHET feedback inhibition; high secretion titers in Pichia pastoris.
swot.w: Cost of large-scale enzyme production and necessity of periodic enzyme re-dosing in open-loop settings.
swot.o: Expanding international plastic treaty compliance mandates and corporate demand for enzymatically circular recycled PET.
swot.t: Competition from emerging chemical depolymerization facilities and regulatory hurdles regarding immobilized biocatalysts in marine zones.
